details.description: 3-species predator-prey chaotic system (Arneodo, Coullet, Tresser; Flake 1998: Computational Beauty of Nature, p. 187). inputs.name: h
inputs.description: Integration time step. Higher values increase rate but cause more instability

details.description: Complex echo-like effect inspired by the classic Eventide unit. A diffuser (similar to JPverb's) connected in a feedback loop with a long modulated delay-line — excels at spacey washes of sound. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: damp
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the delay decays (0..1).

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5). Values below 1 can sound metallic.

inputs.name: diff
inputs.description: Shape of the diffusion unit (0..1). Low values act as a delay-line; medium values build up slowly; >= 0.707 produces smooth exponential decay.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.description: Amount of feedback through the system (0..1). 1.0 produces infinite sustain.

inputs.name: modDepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation (0..1). Combine with modFreq for chorus and pitch variation.

inputs.name: modFreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10).

details.description: Simple cochlear hair cell model (sc3-plugins). Positive input opens ion channels at rate minrate+(input*rate); when accumulated chemicals reach 1.0 the cell fires (output 1.0) then decays each sample by the loss factor. The chemical store is replenished at restorerate; spontaneousrate sets a baseline firing rate; boostrate is how much the input drives chemical flow.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Input to be processed (basilar membrane motion at a particular point pulling an inner hair cell's stereocilia)

inputs.name: spontaneousrate
inputs.description: Spontaneous (baseline) firing rate in Hz — how often the cell fires with no external input

inputs.name: boostrate
inputs.description: Amount that input boosts the chemical flow rate leading to cell fire

inputs.name: restorerate
inputs.description: Rate at which the chemical store is replenished, in Hz

inputs.name: loss
inputs.description: Per-sample decay factor applied after the cell fires

details.description: Algorithmic reverberator inspired by vintage Lexicon and Alesis units. Designed to produce long, lush, chorused reverberation tails — well-suited to synthetic sources rather than realistic spaces. Always outputs stereo.

inputs.name: t60
inputs.description: Approximate reverberation time in seconds (0.1..60). Time for the reverb to decay 60dB when damp == 0; does not affect early reflections.

inputs.name: damp
inputs.description: High-frequency damping as the reverb decays (0..1). 0 = no damping, 1 = very strong.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Scales size of internal delay-lines (0.5..5). Values below 1 can sound metallic.

inputs.name: earlyDiff
inputs.description: Shape of early reflections (0..1). >= 0.707 produces smooth exponential decay; lower values give a slower build-up of echoes.

inputs.name: modDepth
inputs.description: Depth of delay-line modulation (0..1). Combine with modFreq for chorusing.

inputs.name: modFreq
inputs.description: Frequency of delay-line modulation in Hz (0..10). Combine with modDepth for chorusing.

inputs.name: low
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the low band (0..1).

inputs.name: mid
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the mid band (0..1).

inputs.name: high
inputs.description: Multiplier for the reverberation time within the high band (0..1).

inputs.name: lowcut
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between the low and mid bands in Hz (100..6000).

inputs.name: highcut
inputs.description: Crossover frequency between the mid and high bands in Hz (1000..10000).

details.description: Perceptual loudness in sones. Sums excitation in ERB bands with simple spectral and temporal masking, applies equal-loudness contour correction (phons), then phon-to-sone transform. Typical output range 0-64 sones.

inputs.description: FFT chain. Typical FFT size: 1024 (44.1/48kHz) or 2048 (88.2/96kHz)

inputs.name: smask
inputs.description: Spectral masking: per-bin power falloff multiplier for lower bins masking higher bins within ERB bands

inputs.name: tmask
inputs.description: Temporal masking in phons: previous-frame phon level minus tmask competes against new measurement (max wins)

details.description: Live linear-predictive-coding analysis and resynthesis. Models the spectrum of input via an n-sample autocorrelation window and a p-pole LPC filter, then runs source through the derived filter. Best results when source is spectrally flat (impulse train, white noise). Window size n is bounded 1..1024. From sc3-plugins NCAnalysisUGens.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Original signal to analyse with the LPC model

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Excitation signal to filter through the LPC-derived filter

inputs.name: p
inputs.description: Number of poles in the LPC filter

inputs.name: testE
inputs.description: If non-zero, vary the number of poles up to p based on an error condition

inputs.name: delta
inputs.description: Error test threshold (close to but just below 1.0)

inputs.name: windowtype
inputs.description: 0 = rectangular window (abrupt coefficient swap); 1 = triangular window (crossfaded LPCs, smoother but 2x CPU)

details.description: Linear Predictive Coding analysis/resynthesis on 64-sample blocks. Models the input with p coefficients per block and outputs the resynthesised signal — the imperfections of the modelling are the point. From sc3-plugins SLUGens.

Linear Predictive Coding resynthesis. Excites an LPC filter (whose coefficients are stored in `buffer`) with `signal` and reads through the analysis frames at the normalised position `pointer`. Use as the resynthesis side of an LPC analysis/resynthesis pair (cross-synthesis vocoder). From sc3-plugins JoshUGens.

inputs.name: buffer
inputs.description: Buffer holding LPC analysis frames (poles + residuals)

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Excitation signal to drive the LPC filter

inputs.name: pointer
inputs.description: Position to read from analysis frames, 0.0..1.0

details.description: Read residual amplitude, original RMS and pitch from an LPC analysis buffer at a given position. Multi-output: [residual_amp, orig_rms, pitch]. Use to drive a custom excitation in place of the standard LPCSynth excitation. From sc3-plugins JoshUGens.

inputs.name: pointer
inputs.description: Position to read from analysis frames, 0.0..1.0

inputs.name: pointer
inputs.description: Position to read from analysis frames, 0.0..1.0

inputs.name: res
inputs.description: Resonance amount (0 to 1) — values approaching 1 self-oscillate

inputs.name: dist
inputs.description: Distortion drive applied inside the feedback path (0 to 1)

details.description: First-order one-pole low-pass filter. Gentle 6 dB/octave roll-off — ideal as a smoothing stage or for taking the edge off bright sources without colouring the resonance. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

First-order one-pole low-pass filter. Gentle 6 dB/octave roll-off — ideal as a smoothing stage or for taking the edge off bright sources without colouring the resonance. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.
Second order Butterworth low pass filter. Attenuates frequencies above the cutoff frequency.
Second order Butterworth low pass filter. Attenuates frequencies above the cutoff frequency.
Variable-slope six-pole low-pass filter. The slope input morphs the response between gentle and steep cut-off without retuning the cutoff frequency. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

inputs.name: slope
inputs.description: Filter slope (0 to 1) — higher values increase the roll-off steepness

details.description: Variable-slope six-pole low-pass filter. The slope input morphs the response between gentle and steep cut-off without retuning the cutoff frequency. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

inputs.name: slope
inputs.description: Filter slope (0 to 1) — higher values increase the roll-off steepness

details.description: Two point average filter. Implements out(i) = 0.5 * (in(i) + in(i-1)), a simple two-point averager.
Two point average filter. Implements out(i) = 0.5 * (in(i) + in(i-1)), a simple two-point averager.
Two zero fixed lowpass filter. Implements out(i) = 0.25 * (in(i) + 2*in(i-1) + in(i-2)).
Two zero fixed lowpass filter. Implements out(i) = 0.25 * (in(i) + 2*in(i-1) + in(i-2)).

General Linear Time-Invariant filter with arbitrary order. Coefficients are supplied via two buffers — feedback (a) and feedforward (b) — implementing y(n) = sum b_k x(n-k) + sum a_j y(n-j). Stability is the user's responsibility. From sc3-plugins SLUGens.

inputs.name: bufnuma

inputs.name: bufnumb
inputs.description: Buffer number holding feedforward (b) coefficients from previous inputs

details.description: Markov-chain audio resynthesis. While isRecording is non-zero, learns a first-order transition table over the input's amplitude trajectory; once switched off, generates new audio by walking the learned chain. Produces glitchy, granular variations on the source material. By Batuhan Bozkurt. From sc3-plugins BatUGens.

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Input signal to learn from while recording

inputs.name: isRecording
inputs.description: Non-zero to keep learning transitions; zero to freeze the table and synthesize from it

inputs.name: waitTime
inputs.description: Time spent at each Markov state before transitioning, in seconds

inputs.name: tableSize
inputs.description: Number of discrete states in the transition table — higher values track the source more faithfully

details.description: Meddis cochlear inner hair cell model (sc3-plugins). Implements Meddis, Hewitt & Shackleton, 'Implementation details of a computation model of the inner hair-cell/auditory-nerve synapse' (JASA 87(4), April 1990). Hard-coded for the medium-spontaneous-rate parameters; output is scaled by 100 from the JASA paper for sensible audio levels. Functionally similar to half-wave rectification plus low-pass filtering, with a more physiologically plausible mechanism.

inputs.description: Input to be processed (basilar membrane motion at a particular point affecting an inner hair cell's stereocilia)

details.description: Spectral Modeling Synthesis (Serra 1989) — sines+noise model. Tracks sinusoidal partials in the spectrum and models the residual as filtered white noise. Sines and residual can be transformed independently. Assumes block size 64 and 1024-point FFT internally; optimised for 44.1 kHz. Outputs 2 channels (sines and noise). From sc3-plugins NCAnalysisUGens.

inputs.name: maxpeaks
inputs.description: Absolute maximum number of allowed peaks (initialisation only)

inputs.name: currentpeaks
inputs.description: Current number of allowed peaks (modulatable up to maxpeaks)

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: Search tolerance (in spectral bins) for matching peaks across frames

inputs.name: noisefloor
inputs.description: Minimum spectral magnitude for a candidate peak

inputs.name: freqmult
inputs.description: Resynthesis frequency multiplier — multiplies all sinusoidal partials

inputs.name: freqadd
inputs.description: Resynthesis frequency offset — added to all sinusoidal partials

inputs.name: formantpreserve
inputs.description: If non-zero, re-impose the original magnitude envelope when resynthesising (formant preservation) at small CPU cost

inputs.name: useifft
inputs.description: If non-zero, use IFFT-based resynthesis (lower quality but cheaper)

inputs.name: ampmult
inputs.description: Amplitude multiplier — internal compensation for analysis-window power loss

inputs.name: graphicsbufnum
inputs.description: Buffer index for graphics output, or -1 to disable

details.description: Four-times oversampled soft-clipping amplifier. Combines a pregain stage with the SoftClipper4 transfer function — useful as an inline drive/saturation effect. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

inputs.name: pregain
inputs.description: Gain applied to the signal before the soft-clip stage

details.description: Eight-times oversampled soft-clipping amplifier. Combines a pregain stage with the SoftClipper8 transfer function for the smoothest oversampled drive in the pack. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

inputs.name: pregain
inputs.description: Gain applied to the signal before the soft-clip stage

details.description: Four-times oversampled cubic soft clipper. Applies a smooth saturating transfer function with internal upsampling — much cleaner than SuperCollider's stock .softclip when driven hard. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.
Eight-times oversampled cubic soft clipper. Same behaviour as SoftClipper4 with deeper oversampling for the cleanest possible saturation — at higher CPU cost. From sc3-plugins BerlachUGens.

details.description: Vector Base Amplitude Panning (sc3-plugins). Multichannel panner for arbitrary 2D or 3D loudspeaker arrays. Pans a mono source to numChans speakers using the VBAP algorithm by Ville Pulkki — selects the active speaker pair (2D) or triplet (3D) and computes amplitude gains so the perceived source comes from the requested direction. The bufnum input must reference a buffer prepared by VBAPSpeakerArray (loadToBuffer/sendToBuffer) describing the array geometry. Spread (0–100) widens the source from a point to a wider region by activating more speakers.

inputs.name: numChans
inputs.description: Number of output channels (must match the speaker count in the geometry buffer)

inputs.name: bufnum
inputs.description: Buffer holding the speaker geometry data produced by VBAPSpeakerArray.loadToBuffer/sendToBuffer

inputs.name: azimuth
inputs.description: Azimuth angle in degrees, -180 to 180 (0 = front, 90 = left, -90 = right)

inputs.name: elevation
inputs.description: Elevation angle in degrees, -90 to 90 (only meaningful for 3D arrays). Default 0 = horizontal plane

inputs.name: spread
inputs.description: Source spread, 0 to 100. 0 = point source, 100 = signal radiates from all speakers equally

details.description: VOSIM (VOice SIMulation) pulse generator — bursts of squared sinewaves separated by silence, decaying in amplitude. A classic formant-synthesis primitive (Kaegi & Tempelaars, 1978) for vocal-like sounds. Each trigger starts a new burst of nCycles squared-sine cycles at freq, with each cycle scaled by decay relative to the previous one. From sc3-plugins VOSIMUGens.

inputs.name: trig
inputs.description: Trigger — starts a new VOSIM pulse on transition from non-positive to positive (only if no pulse is currently playing). Audio-rate triggering is sample-accurate

inputs.name: freq
inputs.description: Frequency of the squared sinewave inside each burst (Hz)

inputs.name: nCycles
inputs.description: Number of squared sinewave cycles per VOSIM burst — sampled when a new trigger arrives

inputs.name: decay
inputs.description: Per-cycle amplitude decay factor (each cycle's peak is decay times the previous one)

details.description: Window-based amplitude follower. Computes the average absolute value of the input over a sliding window of fixed duration — gives a smoother and less peaky envelope than a one-pole follower. By Batuhan Bozkurt. From sc3-plugins BatUGens.

details.description: Walsh-Hadamard transform — decomposition into square-wave-like basis functions, then reconstruction. Acts as a 64-point block transform; lowest 'which' basis indices are zeroed for filtering effects. From sc3-plugins NCAnalysisUGens.

inputs.name: which
inputs.description: Basis-index threshold — indices below this are zeroed in the reconstruction (0 = pass-through)

details.description: Demand-rate discrete-time neurodynamics simulation. Models the dynamics of a small recurrent neural network with n nodes — initial state x[i], bias theta[i], and an n*n weight matrix between nodes. Transfer function is tanh. Implementation follows Pasemann (2002) 'Complex dynamics and the structure of small neural networks'. From sc3-plugins Neuromodules. Documented as a builder-only entry because the input list is variadic (numChannels, plus n thetas, n initial states, and n*n weights flattened); runtime invocation requires special-case wiring outside the auto-generated bindings.

inputs.name: .x(array)
inputs.description: Array of initial values per node (length numChannels)

inputs.name: .weights(array)
inputs.description: Flattened n*n inter-node weight matrix representing synapses

details.description: Demand-rate tag system — Emil Post's tag system as a demand UGen. The tape size is bounded; recycle/mode controls behaviour on overrun and empty conditions. From sc3-plugins TagSystemUGens. Documented as a builder-only entry because the input list is variadic (axiom and rules arrays are flattened into the input vector).

inputs.description: Set the release time. Accepts seconds or humantime strings.

inputs.name: .perc(attack, release)
inputs.description: Shorthand for percussive envelope - quick attack, natural decay. Clears sustain. Ideal for drums, plucks, piano.

inputs.name: .asr(attack, sustain, release)
inputs.description: Shorthand for attack-sustain-release envelope. Sustain is the level (0-1), not time. Ideal for pads, brass.

inputs.name: .adsr(attack, decay, sustain, release)
inputs.description: Shorthand for full ADSR envelope. Sustain is the level (0-1). Most versatile envelope shape.

inputs.name: .triangle(duration)
inputs.description: Create symmetric triangle envelope - fades in for half duration, fades out for half duration.

inputs.name: .gate(signal)
inputs.description: Set the gate signal that controls envelope triggering. Defaults to constant 1.0 (always on) if not specified.

inputs.name: .time_scale(factor)
inputs.description: Multiply all envelope times by this factor. Use for pitch-dependent decay (lower notes decay longer) or tempo sync.

inputs.name: .level_scale(factor)
inputs.description: Multiply envelope output by this factor. Useful for velocity sensitivity.

inputs.name: .level_bias(offset)

inputs.name: .cleanup_on_finish()
inputs.description: Free the synth when envelope completes (sets done_action=2). Essential for one-shot sounds.

inputs.name: .done_action(value)
inputs.description: Set custom done_action. 0=none, 2=free synth. Use cleanup_on_finish() for common case.
